"Instead of disposing of prunings from winter garden maintenance by burning or shredding, consider transforming them into a dead hedge. This eco-friendly solution not only serves as an effective windbreak but also provides a safe haven for wildlife and a natural division for different sections of your garden. To construct a dead hedge, install stakes or old fence posts in two parallel rows, spaced 50cm apart. Insert larger branches at the bottom and gradually add smaller cuttings, allowing the material to settle over time.

If you're feeling disappointed with your Christmas gifts, you can look forward to the upcoming release of 'The Book of Seeds' (Ivy Press, £30) by Paul Smith, the former head of Kew’s Millennium Seed Bank. Set to publish in February, this exquisite volume showcases over 600 of the world's most peculiar and visually stunning seeds, including a black seed that resembles Donald Trump’s hairstyle and the minuscule seeds of orchids.

For gardeners seeking a touch of winter beauty, consider planting winter-flowering clematis. These resilient climbers can thrive in sunny, sheltered areas, blooming from December to February. Varieties such as Clematis cirrhosa ‘Advent Bells’ and C. cirrhosa var. balearica feature creamy, fragrant blooms with maroon markings, while C. cirrhosa ‘Jingle Bells’ produces pure white flowers. Each variety offers unique charm and can reach impressive heights, providing a delightful spectacle during the colder months." Is there anything else I can help with?
